text:
kevin: Hey folks, quick newbie question. I'm running a quick demo using a hosted API key from my corp laptop and I'm seeing random connection resets during streaming and occasional 429s. Who do I ask for a short live demo quota bump and are there specific MTU/proxy rules IT needs to change?
onboard-bot: Welcome Kevin! :tada: DM dev-support or post here with the demo window. See onboarding checklist: https://redwood.dev/onboarding
dev-support: Hi @kevin 30 we can approve a 24-72h hosted bump for demos. If you need recurring access, request a sandbox/demo key. Please include the demo dates and expected QPS.
it-network: Connection resets + streaming problems often point to proxy TLS termination or MTU fragmentation. Ask IT to allow large chunked responses and ensure the proxy doesn't strip `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`. Also whitelist the egress CIDR and `api.redwood.ai` hostname.
kevin: Here's the curl I ran (streaming test):
```bash
curl -N -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-hosted-FOO" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream -d '{"model":"rwd-1-small","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
```
Got `curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer` sometimes and `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests` other times. When 429s happen headers show `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0` and sometimes no `retry-after`.
sam: If there's no `retry-after`, it might be a token bucket exhaustion on the IP bucket or an internal per-token rate cap. Capture `x-request-id` from the response and paste it here; we can trace it. Also try off-VPN (hotspot) to see if problem persists.
ops-bot: Reminder: do not paste secrets in channels. Please redact the API key in logs and use placeholders.
dev-support: For immediate unblock we can: 1) issue a short-lived sandbox key (separate quota) 2) create ephemeral creds via Vault (we can script a one-off) or 3) approve a hosted demo bump. Which do you prefer?
kevin: Sandbox key would be easiest for now. If sandbox is separate quota, will streaming behave the same?
it-network: Sandbox endpoints are identical in protocol; if your issues are proxy-related they will still appear. For MTU try lowering MSS or ask IT to increase allowed packet size. For corporate proxies that chunk or buffer, ask them to exempt streaming endpoints.
sam: Also check client side: Node/python HTTP clients often buffer; use the raw streaming flag. For curl use `-N` and `--http1.1` to avoid HTTP/2 proxy weirdness during testing.
kevin: Great, DM'ing dev-support for the sandbox key and will try hotspot test. Thanks all! :thumbsup:
